citations.anchor: matches the three config files inference dispatches on
citations.why: Asserts the exported glob is exactly '**/{drizzle.config.ts,ortha.config.ts,package.json}'; the second clause (no target hand-written onto a project) is not asserted anywhere.

citations.anchor: attaches to any project with a drizzle.config.ts, with a cwd-relative config
citations.why: toEqual pins the whole target map produced for a drizzle.config.ts down to executor, cwd, config and cache.

citations.anchor: does not attach db:migrate or db:studio
citations.why: Asserts the inferred target keys for a drizzle.config.ts are exactly ['db:generate'].

citations.anchor: attaches both to the project owning ortha.config.ts, uncached
citations.why: toEqual pins both db:migrate and db:studio onto the ortha.config.ts project, each with cache: false.

citations.anchor: is never cached, and declares no inputs or outputs to be cached against
citations.why: Asserts db:generate has cache === false and neither an `inputs` nor an `outputs` property.

citations.anchor: says it will not fall back to the local defaults
citations.why: db:migrate rejects on an empty URL with the message that names the libpq fall-through it refuses; the sibling case covers an absent URL.

citations.anchor: refuses with one actionable sentence when the URL is %s
citations.why: db:studio rejects for both an empty and an absent URL and asserts runDrizzleKitStudio was never called.

citations.anchor: refuses before building the plugin list
citations.why: Asserts buildPlugins was never called when the URL is empty.

citations.anchor: opens nothing and applies nothing
citations.why: Asserts applyPluginMigrations was never called when the URL is empty.

citations.anchor: applies plugins in exactly the order the host listed them
citations.why: Asserts the sequence of migrationsTable values equals the host's plugin order (skipping plugins without migrations).

citations.anchor: passes each plugin its own folder and tracking table
citations.why: Asserts each plugin is migrated with its own migrationsFolder and its own journal table.

citations.anchor: names the plugin, how far it got, and the order it depends on
citations.why: Asserts the thrown message names the failing plugin, 'applied 2 of 4 plugin(s)', and mentions plugin ORDER.

citations.anchor: still closes the pool
citations.why: Asserts pool.end() ran exactly once on the failure path; the sibling case pins the success path.

citations.anchor: hands drizzle-kit an ephemeral config that never holds the credential
citations.why: Reads the temp config while Studio runs and asserts it contains process.env.DATABASE_URL and neither the password nor the database name.

citations.anchor: passes the URL through the child
citations.why: Asserts the child process env carries DATABASE_URL set to the resolved URL.

citations.anchor: removes the temp directory when Studio exits
citations.why: Asserts the temp config path no longer exists after a clean exit.

citations.anchor: cleans up the temp directory even when Studio fails
citations.why: Asserts the temp config path is gone after drizzle-kit throws — the `finally` half.

citations.anchor: refuses port 0 rather than silently ignoring it
citations.why: Asserts port 0 rejects with 'port 0 is not supported' and that runDrizzleKitStudio was never called.

citations.anchor: warns, naming the exposure and how to undo it
citations.why: Asserts a console.warn naming host:port, 'no authentication' and 'Drop --host' for a non-loopback host; the sibling cases assert silence for loopback. The 'before Studio starts' ordering is not separately asserted.

citations.anchor: exits cleanly when stopped with %s
citations.why: Asserts runDrizzleKitStudio does not throw when the child is killed by SIGINT or SIGTERM, which is what makes the executor return success.

citations.anchor: gives a publishable package build, pack and a redirected nx-release-publish
citations.why: Asserts the three target names for a named package under packages/ that has a tsconfig.lib.json.

citations.anchor: contributes no targets for %s
citations.why: Asserts an empty target object for a manifest outside packages/, the workspace-root manifest, a manifest with no name, and a package with no tsconfig.lib.json.

citations.anchor: contributes no targets for an unparseable manifest, rather than failing the graph
citations.why: Asserts the inference resolves to an empty target object rather than rejecting when package.json will not parse.

citations.anchor: gives a private package build only
citations.why: Asserts a private manifest yields exactly ['build'].

citations.anchor: gives a publishable package build, pack and a redirected nx-release-publish
citations.why: Asserts nx-release-publish equals { executor: '@orthacms/nx:release-publish', options: { packageRoot: 'dist/pack/<projectRoot>' } }; the second clause — that nx.json's targetDefaults declares the same executor — is pinned by nothing.

citations.anchor: gives a publishable package build, pack and a redirected nx-release-publish
citations.why: Asserts targets['pack']['cache'] is false; the 'dist is not among its declared inputs' rationale is not separately asserted.

citations.anchor: waits rather than stealing while a live holder has the lock
citations.why: A second withPublishSlot does not run its publish while a live holder's lock file exists, and only proceeds once the lock is removed.

citations.anchor: holds the lock for the duration and drops it after
citations.why: Asserts the lock file exists inside the publish callback and is gone afterwards.

citations.anchor: evaluates a spacing function only once the slot is held
citations.why: The spacing callback — evaluated immediately before the pause — asserts the lock file already exists, so the gap is waited out under the lock.

citations.anchor: does not remove a lock that is no longer ours
citations.why: After the lock file is overwritten with a foreign pid, the finishing holder leaves it in place — release only removes a lock whose pid matches.

citations.anchor: keeps refreshing the lock while it is held
citations.why: Back-dates the lock mid-publish and asserts the heartbeat has moved its mtime forward again.

citations.anchor: is not stolen from a holder that outlives staleAfter but keeps beating
citations.why: A holder running four times staleAfter while heartbeating is not overlapped by a peer — the peer's publish runs strictly after the holder's.

citations.anchor: steals immediately from a holder that no longer exists
citations.why: With staleAfter at 60s and a lock naming a pid that gives ESRCH, the slot is taken at once and the lock rewritten with this process's pid.

citations.anchor: treats an empty or malformed lock as held, so a genuine race still waits
citations.why: An unparseable lock is not stolen inside staleAfter — the publish does not run until the lock is removed.

citations.anchor: answers unknown for %s
citations.why: A 5xx, a 401 and unparseable JSON all collapse to 'unknown'; the sibling case covers a rejected fetch.

citations.anchor: publishes anyway when the probe could not answer
citations.why: Asserts an 'unknown' probe still reaches publishWithRetry, so a failed probe never fails the publish.

citations.anchor: skips a version the probe says is already on the registry, sending nothing
citations.why: Asserts success with publishWithRetry never called when the probe answers 'version-published'.

citations.anchor: reads a republish of an existing version as success
citations.why: An EPUBLISHCONFLICT from npm is classified 'already-published', which the executor reports as success.

citations.anchor: retries a rate-limited version bump up to the configured ceiling
citations.why: A 429 without creatingName is attempted retries+1 times.

citations.anchor: gives a rate-limited name creation exactly one attempt
citations.why: A 429 with creatingName returns 'creation-blocked' after exactly one execFileSync call.

citations.anchor: records the package that first hit the limit and fails
citations.why: A 'creation-blocked' outcome writes the breaker file naming this package and fails the target.

citations.anchor: makes a later new name bow out without spending a request
citations.why: With the breaker tripped by a peer, a name-absent package fails without calling publishWithRetry and names the package that tripped it.

citations.anchor: does not retry %s
citations.why: E403, ENEEDAUTH and a broken tarball are classified 'failed' rather than 'retryable', so publishWithRetry returns after the first attempt.

citations.anchor: rehearses the publish without probing or waiting
citations.why: Asserts probeRegistry is never called on a dry run and dryRun reaches the publish request; the 'does not wait out the pause' half is not asserted (no timing or spacing assertion).

citations.anchor: uses the environment over the target option
citations.why: With ORTHA_PUBLISH_RETRIES=8 and retries: 2, the value handed to publishWithRetry is 8; sibling cases pin option-over-default and the default.

citations.anchor: accepts 0 from the environment
citations.why: ORTHA_PUBLISH_RETRIES=0 with retries: 2 yields 0, not the option or the default.

citations.anchor: applies the plugins the host built, against the configured URL
citations.why: @orthacms/cli is mocked and applyPluginMigrations is asserted to receive the built plugin list and the URL, so db:migrate cannot carry its own implementation. db:generate's delegation is asserted nowhere (that executor has no spec).

citations.anchor: resolves the URL from the host config
citations.why: @orthacms/cli is mocked and runDrizzleKitStudio is asserted to be called with the resolved URL and options, so db:studio delegates rather than implementing.

citations.anchor: loads the host config and its plugin factory from the workspace root
citations.why: createTsJiti is mocked and its import is asserted to receive both workspace-root paths, so db:migrate loads the host TypeScript through that loader; the legacy-decorator half (lib/jiti.ts has no spec) is unpinned.

citations.anchor: resolves the URL from the host config
citations.why: The same createTsJiti mock is asserted to have loaded the host config, so both executors go through the one shared loader.
